page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-4 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the n1 family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz, configured with 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The server is equipped with 26.0 GB of system memory, yielding 6.5 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates that the server delivers modest processing and memory performance. The single-core and multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng, falls into the bottom 25% tier with scores of 1109.89 and 2914.17 respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show 162.39 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 25.86 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, which also rank in the bottom 25%. Single-threaded gzip compression at 18.93 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 7.06 GB/sec are situated in the bottom 10% tier, reflecting limited single-threaded execution speed.

The primary tradeoff of the n1-highmem-4 is its lower compute performance relative to its memory allocation. With a Geekbench single-core score of 924.0 and a multi-core score of 2032.0, it is less suitable for compute-intensive tasks like large-scale LLM inference, where prompt processing for a small 135M model reaches only 161.98 tokens/sec. However, the 26.0 GB memory capacity provides a qualitative advantage for memory-bound workloads that do not require high CPU throughput, such as caching layers, moderate database operations, or lightweight web serving.
